concept.feedback: The concept satisfies all listed gates. It uses the locally defined checksum success condition appropriately and does not add an unnecessary external job-title criterion.

findings.detail: The premise centers on a midnight-to-dawn watch change, handover board, roster, task order, and handover protocol.
It locally defines the target as the unique participant selected by the six-stream iterated modular checksum under the incident's rules, without relying on an external role definition.
The whiteout, icebound vessel, disrupted equipment, conflicting records, and urgent watch transition provide a coherent operational reason to reconcile evidence.
No participant, name, title, narrative prominence, or early placement identifies the intended answer; selection is explicitly deferred to deterministic evaluation.
The proposal explicitly requires relational, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol statuses and ties each to vessel records and operations.
This is an operational handover and data-integrity reconciliation aboard a research vessel, not a confinement, impossible-entry, or conventional locked-room setup.

final.feedback: The item meets the stated validation criteria.

findings.detail: The story supplies the candidate-specific status facts, the common status-to-integer scale, the accepted tally, and an unambiguous per-candidate checksum procedure, including the reset rule for the counterfactual.
The reader-facing story never identifies any named candidate as satisfying the final concordant-watchkeeper criterion. It discloses only the target tally and the qualification rule.

Each candidate's six statuses are distributed across multiple record paragraphs and evidence types, so the main and counterfactual questions require assembling records rather than relying on a single stated conclusion.
The main and counterfactual questions explicitly request a full name, the intermediate question requests the exact status word, and the scalar question requests the exact integer tally.
Despite the deliberately technical checksum protocol, the Arctic-vessel reconstruction framing makes the records and their categories understandable as part of a coherent story.

story.feedback: deterministic, grounding, and model story critics accept

Deterministic grounding reports all required facts realized exactly once, with no unknown scene obligations.
The evidence is presented as coherent prose paragraphs rather than a table, bullet ledger, or personnel-index wall.
Each candidate receives one nonconflicting status for each of the six named streams.
The main, intermediate, counterfactual, and scalar questions have clear referents and explicitly stated response requirements.
The story states the accepted tally and decision rule but does not directly assert the named main-answer candidate or the counterfactual result.
